agents.title: AI Output Auditor
agents.description: Use to audit generated code, documentation, plans, review comments, or migration proposals for unsupported claims, invented files or APIs, hidden behavior changes, and missing validation.

agents.title: Apt Agent And Skill Steward
agents.description: Use when a canonical agent role or skill is proposed, written, revised, or retired, to confirm it owns a distinct perspective or procedure, is grounded in principles, and is packaged correctly for every platform.

handoffs.when: A new or revised agent or skill has been regenerated into the catalog and platform adapters and must be verified before it is trusted.
required_evidence: the canonical agent or skill file
the regenerated catalog and adapter diffs
npm run check output
handoffs.expected_output: A verification result confirming the catalog, adapters, and validators match the canonical source.

agents.title: Apt AI Agent User Reviewer
agents.description: Use when an autonomous AI agent (not a human) is the one integrating with or acting on the product, to confirm it can act safely and correctly without human-oriented affordances it can't use.

agents.title: Apt AI Consumable API Reviewer
agents.description: Use when an API will be called primarily by AI agents rather than human-written client code, to confirm it's structured for reliable agent consumption.

agents.title: Apt API Architect
agents.description: Use when an API's overall structure — resource model, versioning strategy, service boundaries — needs architectural review, distinct from a single-endpoint contract review.

agents.title: Apt API Bridge Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a bridge or adapter layer sits between a legacy API and a modern one, to confirm it preserves correct behavior on both sides.

agents.title: Apt API Docs Writer
agents.description: Use when API reference material, quickstarts, or integration guides need to be written or reviewed against the actual contract, not just described in prose.

agents.title: Apt API Migration Planner
agents.description: Use when a decision or deliverable must select API styles from audience and behavior, then make contracts predictable, secure, observable, evolvable, and usable by humans and agents, especially when it affects multiple audiences or high-accuracy domains.

agents.title: apt-architect
agents.description: Use when reviewing architecture, repository structure, migration strategy, or harness design before an approach is committed.

agents.title: Apt Architecture Lead
agents.description: Use when a change has structural or system-design implications spanning more than one architecture perspective, and someone needs to own the combined structural verdict.

agents.title: Apt Audience Docs Reviewer
agents.description: Use when documentation exists but it's unclear whether it's actually usable by the audience it claims to serve (beginner, developer, business user, support agent).

agents.title: Apt Bank Acquirer Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a deliverable will be reviewed or used by a bank or acquirer partner, to confirm it addresses their risk, compliance, and settlement concerns.

agents.title: APT Beginner Game Dev Reviewer
agents.description: Use for onboarding, learning plans, setup, architecture explanations, templates, examples, and AI-generated implementation plans.

agents.title: Apt Beginner User Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a deliverable will be seen by someone with no prior context on APT or the product, to confirm it's understandable without assumed background.

agents.title: Apt Business User Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a deliverable will be used by a business owner or operator (not a developer) to run their business, to confirm it matches how they actually think about their operations.

agents.title: Apt Chargeback Risk Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a payment flow, merchant category, or dispute-handling process needs to be assessed for chargeback exposure and evidence-collection readiness.

agents.title: Apt Checkout Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a checkout flow — cart, payment entry, confirmation — needs review for conversion friction and correctness.

agents.title: apt-cloudflare-builder
agents.description: Use when building or reviewing Cloudflare Workers, Pages, Hono, D1, KV, R2, or deployment workflows.

agents.title: apt-code-reviewer
agents.description: Use when code needs a review for bugs, maintainability, behavior preservation, or missing validation.

agents.title: Apt Commerce Experience Reviewer
agents.description: Use when reviewing the broader shopping experience — browsing, cart, post-purchase — beyond the checkout transaction itself.

agents.title: Apt Compliance Awareness Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a change touches data handling, disclosures, or regulated processes, to confirm the team is aware of the compliance obligations involved, even where full legal review is separate.

agents.title: apt-cost-controller
agents.description: Use when a task risks excessive token usage, repeated context loading, unnecessary model escalation, or redundant scans.

agents.title: Apt Crypto Payment Risk Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a payment flow accepts or settles in cryptocurrency and needs review for custody, volatility, and settlement risk.

agents.title: Apt Demo And Diagram Planner
agents.description: Use when a concept, architecture, or workflow needs a demo script or diagram to be understood, and it's unclear what to show, in what order, or at what level of detail.

agents.title: Apt Design Lead
agents.description: Use when a change touches UI, UX flow, or customer-facing design decisions spanning more than one audience or perspective, and someone needs to own the combined design verdict.

agents.title: Apt Developer Integrator Reviewer
agents.description: Use when reviewing the steady-state integration experience for a developer already familiar with the product, to confirm advanced flows and edge cases are covered, not just the first call.

agents.title: Apt Docs Reviewer
agents.description: Use as a general accuracy and completeness pass on any documentation deliverable that doesn't need a specialized audience or API-contract review.

agents.title: Apt Engineering Reviewer
agents.description: Use as a general implementation-quality review of code changes — correctness, maintainability, test coverage — before merge.

agents.title: Apt Execution Lead
agents.description: Use when a change is ready to move from design/architecture into implementation, and someone needs to confirm the plan is buildable, safely sequenced, and verifiable before work starts.

agents.title: Apt Fraud Risk Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a payment flow, fraud rule set, or decline-handling process needs to be assessed for fraud exposure without unnecessarily blocking legitimate transactions.

agents.title: APT Game Architect
agents.description: Use before expansion or when scenes, entities, components, state, input, saves, assets, or services are tangled.

agents.title: APT Game Designer
agents.description: Use when framing play, resolving unclear rules, planning levels, or interpreting player behavior.

agents.title: APT Game Development Coach
agents.description: Use when a learner needs sequencing, plain explanations, project-based exercises, or help recovering from overload.

agents.title: APT Game Docs Writer
agents.description: Use for concepts, design documents, player guides, developer setup, architecture, playtests, releases, or a Game Product Hub.

agents.title: APT Game Prototype Planner
agents.description: Use before implementation or when a team is polishing without answering the main question.

agents.title: APT Game Scope Guardian
agents.description: Use at concept approval, prototype planning, roadmap changes, milestone review, and every game micro-group review.

agents.title: APT Game Testing Reviewer
agents.description: Use before playtests, milestones, releases, or changes to state, saves, inputs, scenes, and core rules.

agents.title: APT Game UI Reviewer
agents.description: Use for menus, HUDs, overlays, settings, onboarding, responsive layouts, and failure/recovery screens.

agents.title: APT Gameplay Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a playable build exists or a proposed change affects moment-to-moment play.

agents.title: Apt Gateway Migration Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a merchant, platform, or integration is migrating from one payment gateway or processor to another, and payment continuity during the cutover is at risk.

agents.title: APT Harness Docs Reviewer
agents.description: Use when reviewing this repository’s own documentation architecture, consistency, source-of-truth boundaries, or operating guidance.

agents.title: Apt Implementation Blueprint Writer
agents.description: Use when a design or architecture decision is approved and needs to become a concrete, step-by-step implementation blueprint an engineer can execute without re-deriving the design.

agents.title: apt-installer
agents.description: Use when applying this repository’s installable agent standards and harness assets to a target repository for the first time.

agents.title: Apt Integration Architect
agents.description: Use when two or more systems need to be connected — via API, event stream, or bridge — and the integration pattern itself needs architectural review.

agents.title: Apt ISV And Tech Partner Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a deliverable will be used by an ISV, plugin provider, or technology partner that connects many merchants to the gateway, to confirm it covers their account linking, attribution, credentials, and installed-base needs, not only the integration build.

handoffs.when: The review shows the partner onboarding or boarding flow itself needs a partner-integration review.
required_evidence: the partner onboarding flow or documentation
the ISV findings that triggered the hand-off
handoffs.expected_output: A partner and acquirer onboarding review of the flow.

agents.title: Apt Launch Readiness Lead
agents.description: Use before a launch or major release, to confirm the product, support, and operational readiness checks are actually complete, not just planned.

agents.title: Apt Merchant Onboarding Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a merchant onboarding flow — signup through first live transaction — needs review for completeness and time-to-first-sale.

agents.title: apt-model-router
agents.description: Use when choosing the smallest sufficient local or cloud model tier for an APT task.

agents.title: Apt Modern API Designer
agents.description: Use when designing a new API from scratch, to confirm it follows current best practice (REST/GraphQL/JSON-RPC as appropriate) rather than replicating legacy patterns.

agents.title: Apt Modernization Architect
agents.description: Use when a legacy system, API, or integration needs a modernization path — replacing SOAP/XML/NVP or monolithic patterns with current APT-supported approaches.

agents.title: Apt New Developer Reviewer
agents.description: Use when reviewing a developer's first-run experience — first API call, first local setup, first error — to confirm nothing assumes prior familiarity with this specific codebase.

agents.title: Apt New Merchant Reviewer
agents.description: Use when reviewing a merchant's first-run experience — signup, KYC, first transaction — to confirm a business owner without payments expertise can complete it unassisted.

agents.title: Apt New Support Agent Reviewer
agents.description: Use when reviewing material a support agent will use to help a customer, to confirm a newly trained agent can resolve common cases without escalating.

agents.title: Apt Payer Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a deliverable affects the person paying a merchant beyond the checkout screen, including receipts, statement descriptors, stored cards, recurring charges, refunds, and disputes, to confirm the payer can recognize, control, and resolve their payments.

handoffs.when: The finding is about the checkout or payment-entry screen itself rather than what happens to the payer after it.
required_evidence: the checkout flow under review
the payer finding that triggered the hand-off
handoffs.expected_output: A checkout experience review of the payment-entry flow.

agents.title: Apt Payment Architect
agents.description: Use when a payment system's structure — gateway abstraction, tokenization boundary, ledger design, or provider failover — needs architectural review before implementation.

agents.title: Apt PRD Writer
agents.description: Use when a feature or initiative needs a PRD written or reviewed — problem, goals, non-goals, success metrics, and scope.

agents.title: Apt Principal
agents.description: Use as the final synthesis step after specialist perspectives have reported, when scattered concerns, risks, and tradeoffs must be reconciled into one accountable, evidence-backed decision with a clear approval status.

agents.title: APT Principles Reviewer
agents.description: Use to review code, documentation, plans, and diffs for APT Core alignment — behavior preservation, clear intent, small reviewable scope with a rollback path, and grounded output with no invented interfaces.

agents.title: Apt Principles Steward
agents.description: Use when a principle, standard, checklist, or workspace-wide rule is proposed, changed, retired, or rolled out to consumer repositories, to own how APT doctrine evolves rather than whether one piece of work follows it.

handoffs.when: A proposed principle or standard change is drafted and needs an alignment review against APT Core before acceptance.
required_evidence: the proposed text and the files it changes
the overlap and conflict analysis against existing principles
handoffs.expected_output: A source-grounded principles review with findings and any conditions or blockers.

handoffs.when: An accepted doctrine change is ready to roll out and its effect on consumer repositories must be measured.
required_evidence: the changed managed files
the affected manifests and consumer list from references/workspace-consumers.json
handoffs.expected_output: A drift and impact report per consumer repository before sync is applied.

agents.title: Apt Product Hub Builder
agents.description: Use when a product or feature area needs a single organized hub page pulling together its scattered docs, specs, and status into one navigable entry point.

agents.title: Apt Refactor Agent
agents.description: Use when code is being restructured without an intended behavior change, to confirm the refactor is actually behavior-preserving.

agents.title: Apt Referral And ISO Partner Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a deliverable will be used by a referral partner, reseller, or independent sales organization (ISO) that brings in or services a merchant portfolio without being the acquiring bank, to confirm it covers attribution, compensation reporting, portfolio visibility, and their limited authority.

handoffs.when: The review touches underwriting, settlement, or risk decisions that belong to the acquiring bank rather than the referral partner or ISO.
required_evidence: the deliverable under review
the decision the partner is being asked to make
handoffs.expected_output: An acquirer-side review of the risk, compliance, and settlement concerns.

agents.title: apt-repair-agent
agents.description: Use when repairing or upgrading an existing APT standards installation while preserving local customizations.

agents.title: apt-repo-scanner
agents.description: Use when inspecting a target repository for installed APT standards, drift, missing files, duplicates, or repair needs.

agents.title: Apt Router
agents.description: Use at the start of any review-council engagement, before any specialist perspective agent is invoked, to decide which agents the request actually needs based on domain, audience, and risk.

handoffs.when: The request requires a substantive review of code, documentation, plans, or diffs for alignment with APT Core.
required_evidence: the artifact or diff under review
the decision context and applicable constraints
handoffs.expected_output: A source-grounded APT principles review with findings, evidence, and any conditions or blockers.

agents.title: apt-security-reviewer
agents.description: Use when reviewing security-sensitive agent, code, configuration, MCP, model-routing, or lifecycle behavior.

agents.title: Apt Support Operations Reviewer
agents.description: Use when a change is about to ship, to confirm the support organization can actually operate and troubleshoot it on day one.

agents.title: APT Task Router
agents.description: Use at the start of a harness engagement to turn a request into a compact, reviewable task packet for the smallest suitable APT workflow.

agents.title: Apt Thinking Lead
agents.description: Use before domain-specific perspectives are engaged, whenever the problem statement, assumptions, or tradeoffs behind a proposal haven't yet been made explicit and checkable.

agents.title: Apt Transaction Intelligence Analyst
agents.description: Use when transaction data, decline patterns, or authorization trends need to be analyzed to explain what's happening and what it implies for risk or revenue.

agents.title: apt-ui-reviewer
agents.description: Use when reviewing UI work for intent, workflow continuity, state design, accessibility, or responsive behavior.

agents.title: apt-verifier
agents.description: Use when outputs, installs, repairs, routing config, or documentation alignment must be verified before they are trusted.

agents.title: Apt Voice Of Customer Analyst
agents.description: Use when raw customer feedback, support tickets, or interview notes need to be synthesized into themes that inform product decisions.

agents.title: Apt Working Backwards Critic
agents.description: Independent sub-agent that scores a Working Backwards package against the versioned rubric plus its declared profile overlay and returns PASS or NEEDS REVISION per stage; must run in a fresh session that authored nothing in the package and writes only critic-review.md and session.json.

agents.title: Apt Working Backwards FAQ Writer
agents.description: Sub-agent invoked by the Working Backwards orchestrator to draft or revise Stage 2, the external FAQ (skeptical customer questions) and the internal FAQ (skeptical engineering, leadership, compliance, and operations questions), using the persona's reviewer agents as lenses.

agents.title: Apt Working Backwards Orchestrator
agents.description: Use to start, resume, or report on a Working Backwards package; it owns session state, stage order, the domain profile and persona, and invokes the writer sub-agents and the independent critic.

handoffs.when: A new package starts, or the press release needs revision after a critic verdict.
required_evidence: feature idea and customer evidence
declared profile and persona
critic feedback when revising

handoffs.when: The press release has passed and the external or internal FAQ is next or needs revision.
required_evidence: the passed press release
the FAQ mode (external or internal)
critic feedback when revising
handoffs.expected_output: A drafted or revised faq-external.md or faq-internal.md.

handoffs.when: Both FAQs have passed and requirements, the engineering handoff, or readiness are next or need revision.
required_evidence: the passed press release and FAQs
open items and blockers
critic feedback when revising
handoffs.expected_output: A drafted or revised requirements.md, engineering-handoff.md, or readiness.md.

handoffs.when: A stage artifact is drafted or revised and needs an independent verdict.
required_evidence: the package folder
the rubric version and declared profile
handoffs.expected_output: critic-review.md and session.json updated with PASS or NEEDS REVISION per stage.

agents.title: Apt Working Backwards Press Release Writer
agents.description: Sub-agent invoked by the Working Backwards orchestrator to draft or revise Stage 1, a customer-centered press release written as if the product has shipped, for the persona and profile recorded in the session.

agents.title: Apt Working Backwards Requirements Writer
agents.description: Sub-agent invoked by the Working Backwards orchestrator to draft or revise Stages 3 and 4, traceable and testable requirements, an engineering handoff of validated increments, and a readiness checklist, all derived only from the passed press release and FAQs.

agents.title: Documentation Normalizer
agents.description: Use to consolidate duplicated, stale, or scattered documentation into canonical homes, proposing a merge, move, and delete plan before any edits.

agents.title: Drack
agents.description: Use when implementation work targets the Cloudflare Workers/Pages + Hono stack, to confirm it follows the stack's actual constraints (bindings, cold starts, edge runtime limits).

agents.title: Glyph
agents.description: Use when a decision or deliverable must select API styles from audience and behavior, then make contracts predictable, secure, observable, evolvable, and usable by humans and agents, especially when it affects multiple audiences or high-accuracy domains.

agents.title: Intent UX Reviewer
agents.description: Use to review a product surface through user intent, workflow completion, state design, accessibility, and responsive behavior.

agents.title: Javik
agents.description: Use as the senior cross-cutting sign-off for architecture work, after specialist architecture perspectives (api, integration, modernization) have reported, to reconcile them into one accountable structural recommendation.

agents.title: Kaidan
agents.description: Use when a partner or acquirer integration/onboarding flow needs review, distinct from a single merchant's onboarding.

agents.title: Kasumi
agents.description: Use when a change has security implications — authentication, data exposure, attack surface — that need review before it ships.

agents.title: Miranda
agents.description: Use when prioritization, sequencing, or tradeoff decisions across multiple initiatives need a product-management perspective.

agents.title: Samara
agents.description: Use when a change affects who can do what — roles, scopes, access control rules — to confirm the permission model is correct and least-privilege.

agents.title: Suvi
agents.description: Use when a product is evaluating or building stablecoin acceptance or settlement, to confirm operational and compliance readiness before launch.

agents.title: Wrex
agents.description: Use as the senior cross-cutting sign-off for payments work, after specialist payment perspectives (fraud, chargeback, gateway, architecture) have reported, to reconcile them into one accountable payments recommendation.
